THE FRAMEWORK

Product-Led Growth:
the product sells itself

PLG is a go-to-market strategy where the product is the primary driver of acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion. Slack, Figma, Notion and Dropbox all got here without a traditional sales team.

✗ SALES-LED GROWTH

✗High CAC — you pay for every user
✗Long cycles — demos, contracts, procurement
✗Value arrives weeks after signup
✗Growth depends on headcount

✓ PRODUCT-LED GROWTH

✓Low CAC — product acquires users
✓The product IS the demo
✓Habit-forming from day one
✓Scales without a sales army

THE TOOLKIT

Frameworks that make it work

[PLG-01]

NORTH STAR METRIC

One metric that captures the value delivered to users. Everything aligns to it. Slack: messages sent. Zoom: meeting minutes. I help teams find this number first.

STRATEGY

[PLG-02]

ACTIVATION MAPPING

Find the exact actions in the first 48h that predict 30-day retention. Build onboarding around those moments — cohort analysis, not gut feeling.

ANALYTICS

[PLG-03]

FREEMIUM ARCHITECTURE

What to gate and what to give free is a design decision. The free tier must deliver real value while creating natural urgency to upgrade.

MONETIZATION

[PLG-04]

VIRAL LOOP DESIGN

Figma is free to collaborate — that's a viral loop baked into the core. Design the product to be better when shared. Incentive is functionality, not cash.

GROWTH

[PLG-05]

PQL SCORING

Know when a free user is ready to buy based on product behavior — not whether they opened your email. PQLs convert 3x better than MQLs.

CONVERSION

[PLG-06]

AI-POWERED ONBOARDING

Generative AI can personalize onboarding paths in real time. Every user takes a different route to their AHA moment — the new frontier of PLG.

AI + PLG

LEADERSHIP · Jan 2021

THE THREE PILLARS OF EFFECTIVE LEADERSHIP

▼

Leadership is one of the most challenging yet rewarding soft skills to develop. Real-world application is what truly refines it — requiring introspection, emotional intelligence, and continuous improvement.

1. COMMUNICATE CLEARLY

Effective communication is the foundation. Agile structures this with stand-ups, retrospectives, and sprint reviews. My preferred model is Radical Candor — challenging directly while caring personally.

2. MOTIVATE THE TEAM

"If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together." — Cory Booker

Great leadership fosters collaboration, trust, and accountability. Cultivate psychological safety where ideas and concerns can be shared openly.

3. DELIVER RESULTS

Leadership is ultimately about outcomes. Align on clear goals, adapt when plans change, maintain accountability without stifling creativity.

"To improve is to change; to be perfect is to change often." — Churchill
LEADERSHIP · TEAMS · COMMUNICATION

CREATIVITY · Jan 2021

ON FOSTERING CREATIVITY IN PRODUCT TEAMS

▼

Creativity integrates curiosity, flexibility, and design thinking to generate value from seemingly insignificant ideas. It thrives in environments that encourage diversity, open communication, and a culture of empathy.

HOW TO CULTIVATE IT

  • Foster genuine interest in the problem at hand
  • Ensure creative contributions are valued by leadership
  • Maintain childlike curiosity — approach problems with fresh eyes
  • Produce many ideas, then filter effectively

A worthwhile goal is to create something truly original that endures. That starts with making it safe to fail.

CREATIVITY · DESIGN THINKING · TEAMS

PRODUCT · Jan 2021

WHAT I LEARNED MANAGING PRODUCT ACROSS 4 INDUSTRIES

▼

From fintech to telco to retail and education, the pattern is always the same: align on clear goals, adapt when plans change, and maintain accountability without stifling creativity.

WHAT NEVER CHANGES

  • Prioritization is always hard and always necessary
  • Stakeholder alignment takes more time than you budget
  • The best discoveries come from talking to actual users
  • Agile is a culture first — ceremonies come second
PRODUCT MANAGEMENT · AGILE · LEADERSHIP

UX · Jan 2021

UX PRINCIPLES I APPLY TO EVERY PRODUCT

▼

UX design focuses on the feel of a product — ensuring interactions are intuitive, seamless, and meaningful. A product that users can't understand quickly is a product that fails, regardless of the engineering.

WHAT MAKES A PRODUCT WORK

  • Useful — Simple, easy to use, designed with familiarity in mind
  • Usable — Addressing a real need in the user's life
  • Desirable — Visually appealing, evoking positive emotions

At Elektra we delivered 900+ wireframes in 3 months — only because we had clear UX principles guiding every prioritization call in every sprint.
